articles.headline: NFL Week 2 betting guide: Top plays for Sunday afternoon's games
articles.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 2 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
articles.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 1.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Jump to:

Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props

Bowen's Game of the Week

Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans (-2.5, 46.5)

1 p.m. ET on CBS, Reliant Stadium, Houston

This line has fluctuated but at -2.5, I am all-in. Would I feel the same at -3? I wouldn't love it, but I'd be willing to bet Houston at home in a bounce-back game after the Week 1 loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Let's get into what to look for on both sides of the ball, and we'll finish with some props bets to play.

When Houston has the ball: Houston spent the offseason working on its run game, trading for David Montgomery and adding to the offensive front. And we saw a dedicated effort to run the football in Week 1, as Montgomery had 20 carries, with Woody Marks chipping in with nine. Now, was it super efficient? No. Montgomery averaged just 3.0 YPC, and the Texans registered a run block win rate of 74% (17th in the league). But it's clear that Houston wants the run game to be a foundational element of its offense. This can boost the passing opportunities for quarterback C.J. Stroud, who will see a Bengals defense featuring a rebuilt front anchored by defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II and an underrated secondary that can mix both zone and man looks. I would look for play-action concepts (which mirror the run game) to attack the Bengals' two-deep zone shells while also scheming up some shot plays. With Nico Collins out, the scheme won't change in Houston. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte can work the interior in-breakers while Jaylin Noel operates out of the slot. I truly think Houston looks to control the tempo on offense in this one, but let's keep an eye on third downs because the Texans need to beat man coverage from the Bengals there.

When Cincinnati has the ball: I want to see this matchup against the Texans' defense. Though the Bengals looked flat in a Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Joe Burrow finished with 254 yards passing, and Ja'Marr Chase had two receptions for 12 yards), they create conflict because of scheme and talent

articles.headline: Acuña grand slam leads Braves to 6-3 win, dropping Astros from AL West lead
articles.description: — Ronald Acuña Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat Houston 6-3 Saturday night to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead.
articles.headlineJa: アクーニャの満塁弾でブレーブスが6-3で勝利、アストロズはア・リーグ西地区首位から転落
articles.descriptionJa: 7回にロナルド・アクーニャ・ジュニアが勝ち越し満塁ホームランを放ち、アトランタ・ブレーブスが土曜日の夜にヒューストンを6-3で破り、アストロズをア・リーグ西地区首位から引きずり下ろした。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Ronald Acuña Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and the Atlanta Braves beat Houston 6-3 Saturday night to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead.


              Houston (77-78) fell one game behind Texas (78-77) and trails the Chicago White Sox (79-76) by two games for the last AL wild card. The Astros had held at least a share of the division lead each day since Aug. 25.


              Atlanta assured its eighth playoff berth in nine seasons on Friday and is in position to clinch its first NL East title since 2023 on Sunday.


              Trailing 2-1, Atlanta loaded the bases against AJ Blubaugh (5-3) and Acuña homered off Bryan Abreu for his second grand slam this season and the fifth of his big league career.


              Acuña singled and walked twice in his first three plate appearances. He has homered in three of his last four games.


              Mike Yastrzemski added a solo homer in the eighth inning.


              Grant Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs and eight hits over six innings.


              Yainer Diaz hit an RBI double in the eighth off Dylan Lee, who struck out pinch-hitter Nelson Velázquez to end the inning.


              Raisel Iglesias pitched a perfect ninth inning for his 34th save in 37 chances.


              Jose Altuve had three hits for Houston, while Isaac Paredes was 2 for 3 with a home run, walk and two RBI.


              Christian Walker had two hits after entering the game hitless in his previous 23 at-bats.


              Hayden Wesneski allowed one run on four hits over 5 1/3 innings.


              Up next
              Astros RHP Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) and Braves LHP Martín Pérez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) start Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Rangers take sole possession of AL West lead, Quantrill leaves with injury in 6-3 win over Blue Jays
articles.description: — Five relievers held Toronto to six hits after Cal Quantrill left 12 pitches in because of right lat tightness, and the Rangers moved into sole possession of the AL West lead for the first time since late August with a 6-2 win over the Blue Jays on...
articles.headlineJa: レンジャーズがブルージェイズに6-3で勝利しア・リーグ西地区の単独首位に浮上、クアントリルは負傷降板
articles.descriptionJa: カル・クアントリルが右広背筋の張りにより12球で降板した後、5人の救援陣がトロントを6安打に抑え、レンジャーズはブルージェイズに6-2で勝利して8月下旬以来となるア・リーグ西地区の単独首位に立った...
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Five relievers held Toronto to six hits after Cal Quantrill left 12 pitches in because of right lat tightness, and the Rangers moved into sole possession of the AL West lead for the first time since late August with a 6-2 win over the Blue Jays on Saturday night.


              Texas (78-77) has won six of seven and moved a half-game ahead of Houston (77-78), which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers have a winning record for the first time since before play on Aug. 11.


              Jordan Montgomery (1-0) got his first win since Aug. 14, 2024, pitching 3 2/3 hitless innings. He returned from Tommy John surgery this past Aug. 9.


              Davis Schneider hit a pinch-homer for the AL champion Blue Jays (76-79), who have lost eight of 12. They trail the Chicago White Sox by three games for the AL’s final wild card.


              Quantrill a, son former Toronto All-Star Paul Quantrill, retired George Springer on a groundout opening the second inning and didn’t appear to exhibit any pain but didn’t face another batter. The 31-year-old right-hander left his previous start on Sept. 13 at Arizona after 70 pitches because of a sore back.


              Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said after the game he had no update on Quantrill, who is to have an MRI on Sunday.


              Quantrill was followed by Montgomery, and Nathan Eovaldi, Robert Garcia, Chase Silseth and Jacob Latz pitched one inning each.


              Texas scored twice in the second off José Soriano (12-8) without a base hit, helped by a walk, hit batter, infield throwing error and a wild pitch.


              Texas’ three-run sixth featured an RBI double by Wyatt Langford when left fielder Myles Straw pulled up as the ball land between him and the wall.


              Soriano allowed six runs — five earned — pitching three batters into the sixth.


              UP NEXT


              Rangers RHP Jacob deGrom (11-9, 3.79), who is 8-2 at home this season with a .183 opponents batting average, starts Sunday while the Blue Jays employ a bullpen game.


              ------

articles.headline: Brandon Lowe's go-ahead homer in the 8th lifts the Pirates past the Royals, 6-5
articles.description: — Brandon Lowe hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth to lift the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 6-5 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: 8回にブランドン・ロウが勝ち越し弾、パイレーツが6-5でロイヤルズを下す
articles.descriptionJa: ブランドン・ロウが8回に勝ち越しの2ランホームランを放ち、ピッツバーグ・パイレーツが土曜日の夜にカンザスシティ・ロイヤルズに6-5で勝利した。
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- — Brandon Lowe hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth to lift the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 6-5 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Saturday night.


              Lowe jumped on a pitch from Steven Cruz (2-4) and sent it into the seats in right field for his 33rd homer of the season, the second-most by a player in their first year with the Pirates. The two-time All-Star was acquired by Pittsburgh last winter. 


              The home run was also the 96th at PNC Park this year for the Pirates, a club record for most homers at home in a season. The 1947 club hit 95 round-trippers when the team called Forbes Field home.


              Pittsburgh rookie outfielder Ronnie Simon hit his first career homer. Jake Mangum added his fifth of the season as the Pirates won their third straight to improve to 78-77. The franchise is seeking its first winning season since 2018.


              Lowe, Rafael Flores and Oneil Cruz had two hits each for the Pirates. Luke Weaver (3-1) picked up the win by pitching a scoreless eighth. Mason Montgomery worked the ninth for his 15th save. Montgomery hasn't allowed a run in 22 2/3 innings, the second-longest streak ever by a Pittsburgh reliever.


              Nick Loftin had four hits for the Royals. Bobby Witt Jr. added three and Carter Jensen slugged his 25th of the season but it wasn't enough to prevent the Royals from losing for the sixth time in seven games.


              Pirates starting pitcher Bubba Chandler needed 90 pitches to get through four innings. The 24-year-old right-hander allowed three runs with a walk and six strikeouts.


              Up next
              The series wraps up Sunday. Michael Wacha (9-9, 3.34 ERA) was set to start for the Royals. The Pirates had not announced a starter.


              ------

articles.headline: Boyd ends 6-start winless streak, Cubs beat Reds 5-2 to close on playoff berth
articles.description: — Matthew Boyd ended a six-start winless streak, Dansby Swanson hit his first home run since coming off the injured list and the Chicago Cubs moved closer to their second straight playoff berth by beating the Cincinnati Reds 5-2 Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ボイドが先発6試合ぶりの白星、カブスがレッズを5-2で破りプレーオフ進出に前進
articles.descriptionJa: マシュー・ボイドが先発6試合連続未勝利を終わらせ、ダンスビー・スワンソンが故障者リスト復帰後初となる本塁打を放ち、シカゴ・カブスは土曜日にシンシナティ・レッズを5-2で破り、2年連続のプレーオフ進出に近づいた。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- — Matthew Boyd ended a six-start winless streak, Dansby Swanson hit his first home run since coming off the injured list and the Chicago Cubs moved closer to their second straight playoff berth by beating the Cincinnati Reds 5-2 Saturday.


              Michael Busch hit a tiebreaking home run off Nick Lodolo (3-6) in the sixth inning for a 3-2 lead, reaching 20 homers for the third time in four seasons.


              Swanson added a ninth-inning drive against Zach McCambley, Swanson's home run and first since Aug. 12. Swanson returned Friday from a strained left oblique that had sidelined him since Aug. 16.


              Chicago (86-69), which leads the major leagues with 214 home runs, began the day tied with Philadelphia and San Diego for the three NL wild cards.


              Boyd (9-5) had been been 0-4 since beating Kansas City on Aug. 9. He allowed two runs — one earned — and two hits in five innings as part of a four-hitter.


              Lodolo gave up three runs and six hits in seven innings for the Reds, who have lost nine of 12.


              Matt Shaw's sacrifice fly in the second and Seiya Suzuki RBI single in the fifth built a 2-0 lead.


              Cincinnati tied the score in the bottom half on Swanson's run-scoring throwing error at shortstop and . Ke’Bryan Hayes' RBI single.


              Nico Hoerner added a run-scoring single in the eighth.


              Up Next
              Cubs LHP David Peterson (8-8, 5.11) and Reds LHP Rhett Lowder (6-11, 5.79) start Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 uniforms: Rams debut 'Classic Sol,' Ravens go all-white
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 2, led by a new alternate look from the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週のユニフォーム：ラムズは「クラシック・ソル」を初披露、レイブンズはオールホワイト
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・ラムズの新しいオルタネイト・ユニフォームをはじめ、NFL各チームが第2週に着用するユニフォームを紹介。
articles.body:
Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history.

Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white.

The Baltimore Ravens underwent a closet redesign in the offseason, and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. 

It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers, who will wear their traditional home green on the road.

In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign.
